answer: New identities pay a full bond plus a decaying ember fee that burns on registration, making mass signups expensive. Each agent must stake a rare plot token, like a saffron-tinted orchard deed, to join an epoch. Existing peers co-sign only after sustained useful work, so fake accounts stay cold and unbonded. An attacker needs thousands of costly deeds and burned fees, while honest participants recover stake through verified contributions. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
